To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the modeling procedures and program packages presented in this article can model water flow through soils in a manner that is mathematically as accurate as the most advanced modeling procedures that are currently used in soil mechanics and soil physics.

(1) the modeling techniques described in this article can model the water flow in soils with a similar accuracy as previous models for linear problems, (2) the modeling techniques can also be used for modeling water flow in soils that are non-linear, non-homogeneous, non-isothermal, anisotropic, non-isotropic and time-dependent, (3) the modeling procedures and modules are available in the form of computer programs, which can be used to simulate water flow in two and three dimensional

(1) the modeling procedures discussed here, which are applicable for two-dimensional and three-dimensional problems, can be used for a variety of soil processes and (2) the modeling procedures are accurate enough to be applied to practical situations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mathematical models and computer programs to simulate the flow and transport of water and solutes through soils.
developing and validating mathematical models for water flow in soils.

the development of modeling procedures and computer programs for the simulation of water flow and related phenomena in two- and/or three-dimensional applications, where non-linearity, heterogeneity, and time dependency can be experienced.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
modeling of water flow is a difficult task, but not impossible.
the modeling techniques described in this article are capable of modeling the physical mechanisms in soil, which can be defined in quantitative terms.
the mathematical modeling techniques presented here are applicable to most of the physical processes that can be defined quantitatively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a modeling system which can simulate water, salt, and thermal flow in two- or three-dimensional soils with a high degree of mathematical accuracy and flexibility.
the modeling of soil-water interactions can be performed in a rigorous and quantitative way.
we have demonstrated the feasibility of modeling most physical processes in soils, which can be defined in quantitative terms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mathematical accuracy of these modeling techniques is not the main limitation to their application in practical field problems, rather it is the availability of the necessary information to define the soil parameters in the model.

it is possible to develop a modeling framework for water flow that is sufficiently general to model the wide range of soil physical behavior observed in the field, and yet sufficiently simple that the model can be applied with confidence to a wide range of field situations.
it is possible to model most of the complex processes in soils, if we have the right modeling tools.
